lines.text: Seven pointy tips on a star. What do their angles add up to?
lines.caption: Seven pointy tips on a star. What do their angles add up to?

lines.text: You don't need to measure a single one. A walking pencil can tell us!
lines.caption: You don't need to measure a single one. A walking pencil can tell us!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's add up some star points.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's add up some star points.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Seven points are evenly spaced on a circle.
lines.caption: Seven points are evenly spaced on a circle.

lines.text: A star is drawn by joining each point to the second point after it, going around the circle.
lines.caption: A star is drawn by joining each point to the second point after it, going around the circle.

lines.text: What is the sum, in degrees, of the seven angles at the tips of the star?
lines.caption: What is the sum, in degrees, of the seven angles at the tips of the star?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? Each line skips one point. A joins to C, C joins to E, and so on.
lines.caption: So what do we know? Each line skips one point. A joins to C, C joins to E, and so on.

lines.text: The star is perfectly even, so all seven tips are the same size.
lines.caption: The star is perfectly even, so all seven tips are the same size.

lines.text: We want the total of all seven tip angles.
lines.caption: We want the total of all seven tip angles.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: cut the circle into slices from the center.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: cut the circle into slices from the center.

lines.text: Seven equal slices fill the whole turn. Call each slice angle s.
lines.caption: Seven equal slices fill the whole turn. Call each slice angle s.

lines.text: Seven copies of s make three hundred sixty degrees.
lines.caption: Seven copies of s make three hundred sixty degrees.

lines.text: Now zoom in on the tip at A. Its two lines go to C and to F.
lines.caption: Now zoom in on the tip at A. Its two lines go to C and to F.

lines.text: Draw lines from the center to A and to C. The angle at the center covers two slices, so it's two s.
lines.caption: Draw lines from the center to A and to C. The angle at the center covers two slices, so it's two s.

lines.text: Both of those lines are radii, so they're equal. Triangle O A C is isosceles.
lines.caption: Both of those lines are radii, so they're equal. Triangle O A C is isosceles.

lines.text: Its angles add to one hundred eighty. Subtract two times the letter s, then split the rest in half.
lines.caption: Its angles add to one hundred eighty. Subtract two times the letter s, then split the rest in half.

lines.text: So each base angle is ninety minus s.
lines.caption: So each base angle is ninety minus s.

lines.text: The other side works the same way. Triangle O A F has a two s angle at the center too.
lines.caption: The other side works the same way. Triangle O A F has a two s angle at the center too.

lines.text: So its angle at A is also ninety minus s.
lines.caption: So its angle at A is also ninety minus s.

lines.text: So the tip at A is ninety minus s, twice. That's one hundred eighty minus two s.
lines.caption: So the tip at A is ninety minus s, twice. That's one hundred eighty minus two s.

lines.text: Seven tips make seven times one hundred eighty, minus fourteen times s.
lines.caption: Seven tips make seven times one hundred eighty, minus fourteen times s.

lines.text: That's one thousand two hundred sixty, minus fourteen s.
lines.caption: That's one thousand two hundred sixty, minus fourteen s.

lines.text: Fourteen times s is two times seven times s.
lines.caption: Fourteen times s is two times seven times s.

lines.text: That's two times three hundred sixty, which is seven hundred twenty.
lines.caption: That's two times three hundred sixty, which is seven hundred twenty.

lines.text: One thousand two hundred sixty minus seven hundred twenty is five hundred forty.
lines.caption: One thousand two hundred sixty minus seven hundred twenty is five hundred forty.

lines.text: The tips add up to five hundred forty degrees. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: The tips add up to five hundred forty degrees. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Here's a really clever way. Put a pencil at A, pointing at C, and walk it around the star.
lines.caption: Here's a really clever way. Put a pencil at A, pointing at C, and walk it around the star.

lines.text: At each tip, the pencil turns to head down the next line.
lines.caption: At each tip, the pencil turns to head down the next line.

lines.text: The turn and the tip angle sit on a straight line, so together they make one hundred eighty.
lines.caption: The turn and the tip angle sit on a straight line, so together they make one hundred eighty.

lines.text: Each line jumps two slices. Seven lines make fourteen slices: two full circles.
lines.caption: Each line jumps two slices. Seven lines make fourteen slices: two full circles.

lines.text: Watch the pencil go all the way round. It circles the center twice before it gets home!
lines.caption: Watch the pencil go all the way round. It circles the center twice before it gets home!

lines.text: Two full circles means two times three hundred sixty degrees of turning. That's seven hundred twenty.
lines.caption: Two full circles means two times three hundred sixty degrees of turning. That's seven hundred twenty.

lines.text: At each of the seven tips, the tip plus the turn is one hundred eighty.
lines.caption: At each of the seven tips, the tip plus the turn is one hundred eighty.

lines.text: Seven times one hundred eighty is one thousand two hundred sixty.
lines.caption: Seven times one hundred eighty is one thousand two hundred sixty.

lines.text: The turns use up seven hundred twenty. So the tips get the rest.
lines.caption: The turns use up seven hundred twenty. So the tips get the rest.

lines.text: One thousand two hundred sixty minus seven hundred twenty is five hundred forty again!
lines.caption: One thousand two hundred sixty minus seven hundred twenty is five hundred forty again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? For any star, just count how many times the pencil circles the center.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? For any star, just count how many times the pencil circles the center.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice A, one hundred eighty, is the famous answer for a five-point star. Seven points is a different star!
lines.caption: Choice A, one hundred eighty, is the famous answer for a five-point star. Seven points is a different star!

lines.text: Choice E, nine hundred, is the angle total for an ordinary seven-sided shape.
lines.caption: Choice E, nine hundred, is the angle total for an ordinary seven-sided shape.

lines.text: The pencil would circle only once.
lines.caption: The pencil would circle only once.

lines.text: Choice D, seven hundred twenty, is the total turning of the pencil, not the tips.
lines.caption: Choice D, seven hundred twenty, is the total turning of the pencil, not the tips.

lines.text: Choice B, three hundred sixty, is one full turn.
lines.caption: Choice B, three hundred sixty, is one full turn.

lines.text: That's what the turns of an ordinary shape add to, not a star's tips.
lines.caption: That's what the turns of an ordinary shape add to, not a star's tips.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Don't use a rule you remember for a different shape. Check it.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Don't use a rule you remember for a different shape. Check it.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same seven points, but now join each point to the third point after it.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same seven points, but now join each point to the third point after it.

lines.text: The star gets pointier. What do its seven tip angles add up to?
lines.caption: The star gets pointier. What do its seven tip angles add up to?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's walk the pencil. Each line now jumps three slices, and seven lines make twenty-one slices.
lines.caption: Let's walk the pencil. Each line now jumps three slices, and seven lines make twenty-one slices.

lines.text: Twenty-one slices is three full circles.
lines.caption: Twenty-one slices is three full circles.

lines.text: So the pencil turns three times three hundred sixty, which is one thousand eighty degrees.
lines.caption: So the pencil turns three times three hundred sixty, which is one thousand eighty degrees.

lines.text: Tips plus turns is still seven times one hundred eighty, one thousand two hundred sixty.
lines.caption: Tips plus turns is still seven times one hundred eighty, one thousand two hundred sixty.

lines.text: One thousand two hundred sixty minus one thousand eighty is one hundred eighty degrees!
lines.caption: One thousand two hundred sixty minus one thousand eighty is one hundred eighty degrees!

lines.text: Here's the sneaky part. Pointier tips, so a smaller total. If you got one hundred eighty, amazing work!
lines.caption: Here's the sneaky part. Pointier tips, so a smaller total. If you got one hundred eighty, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: At every corner, the tip and the pencil's turn add to one hundred eighty.
lines.caption: At every corner, the tip and the pencil's turn add to one hundred eighty.

lines.text: Count how many times the pencil circles the center. Times three hundred sixty is the total turning, and the tips get the rest.
lines.caption: Count how many times the pencil circles the center. Times three hundred sixty is the total turning, and the tips get the rest.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
